description: Issue #957 adversarial review finding F1 (#960): neutralizes DashboardCredentialMasking.ReconcileWidgetHeaders' host-scoping guard by forcing `sameDestination` to always be `true` via a compile-preserving `true || (...)` prefix (mirrors the established `false &&`/`true ||` short-circuit pattern already used by the 948-dashboard-restoptions-egress-write-guard-neutralize mutant -- not a compile-time constant since the right-hand operands are runtime property/method results, so no CS0162 unreachable-code warning). This reintroduces the F1 credential-forwarding defect: an editor who merely retypes a REST widget's URL through the shipped designer (which has no headers-editing UI at all and always omits the headers key) would have the widget's REAL stored credential silently carried over to whatever new host they typed, with nothing logged and no confirmation -- the very next viewer/background fetch sends that credential to the new, caller-chosen destination. This is the exact attack script the F1 fix closes (see DashboardCredentialMasking.ReconcileWidgetHeaders's own XML remarks and docs/production-readiness.md's #957 entry). red_tests below cover: the cross-host case (a) drop, the cross-host case (d) sentinel-must-not-restore, three distinct 'different destination' shapes (port, scheme, unparseable/empty URL on either side), and the full end-to-end attack-script reproduction through the real controller. green_test is ReconcileWidgetHeaders_case_a_same_host_different_path_still_preserves_headers, which proves the underlying same-host preserve semantics -- the common, legitimate case F1 must not break -- still work; it is unaffected by this mutation because forcing sameDestination=true does not change the outcome for an already-same-destination pair.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Dashboard.Dash: Expected dictionary to be <null> because stored credentials must not silently follow a widget to a different destination
Expected string not to be <null> because there is no value stored for the NEW destination to restore
Expected dictionary to be <null> because different port is a different destination
Expected dictionary to be <null> because http vs https is a different destination even for the same host
Expected dictionary to be <null> because an unparseable incoming URL must never be treated as 'same destination'
Expected dictionary to be <null>, but found \{\["Authorization"\] = "Bearer real-token"\}
Expected dictionary to be <null>, but found \{\["Authorization"\] = "Bearer real-token"\}
Expected collection to be null or empty because the real credential bound to api\.vendor\.com must NOT have been carried over to evil\.example

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured by applying the patch manually and running exactly as run_mutant.py does (`dotnet build -c Release` then `dotnet test -c Release --no-restore --filter <red_test_filter>`) before writing this file, then reverting the manual patch application and letting run_mutant.py apply/run/revert it itself for the actual gate run. All eight declared red_tests failed with exactly the messages the patterns above match (dictionary/string/collection null-or-content assertions naming the specific F1 scenario each test targets). Also ran the full DashboardCredentialMasking*Tests filter (47 tests) under the same mutant beforehand to confirm the failure set was EXACTLY these eight and no others -- every other test (including all same-host, case (b)/(c), and case (f) tests) stayed green, confirming the mutation's blast radius matches what is declared here.
